CLINICAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DATE OF BIRTH: [redacted]
MEDICAL RECORD: [redacted ID]
REFERRING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE OF REPORT: [redacted]

REFERRAL REASON
Mutation screening of ARX gene in pediatric male patient with suspected neurological condition associated with ARX mutations.

METHODOLOGY
DNA sequencing of ARX gene, including all coding exons and splice sites. Reference sequence NM_139058 used. Analysis included specific evaluation of poly-alanine tracts at nucleotides c.297 and c.429, which represent hotspots for pathogenic expansions. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. PCR amplification and bidirectional Sanger sequencing were performed for all 5 exons of the ARX gene with minimum coverage of 20x. Special attention was given to the GC-rich regions containing the poly-alanine tracts using optimized PCR conditions.

RESULTS
ARX gene (NM_139058.2): No pathogenic variants detected

Poly-alanine tract analysis:
- Tract 1 (c.297): 16 repeats (normal range: 12-16)
- Tract 2 (c.429): 12 repeats (normal range: 7-12)

No poly-alanine tract expansion mutations detected. Normal repeat lengths observed in both poly-alanine tracts. No sequence variants identified throughout the coding regions or splice sites.

Quality metrics:
- All exons successfully amplified and sequenced
- Minimum coverage: 20x
- Average coverage: 45x
- Poly-alanine regions confirmed by repeat analysis

SUMMARY
Comprehensive sequencing of the ARX gene revealed no pathogenic variants. The two poly-alanine tracts showed normal repeat lengths with no evidence of expansion mutations. Common ARX mutations including c.304ins(GCG)7, c.333ins(GCG)10, and splice site variants were specifically excluded. Based on these results, the patient's symptoms are very unlikely due to ARX gene mutation. The sensitivity of this test for detecting point mutations and small insertions/deletions is >99%. Large deletions or duplications would not be detected by this methodology.

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
